## New Features

- Added a built-in Google Cloud Vertex AI provider, configured with `model_provider = "gcp"`. (#56265)
- Added GPT-6.1 Terra to the model catalogs. (#57337)
- Added a repository filter to the session picker and directory grouping to the agent command center, making it easier to navigate sessions across linked worktrees. (#56308)
- Added experimental attached thread forks to the app-server API. (#56351)
- Enabled reasoning effort changes during a conversation by default for supported models. (#56163)
- Enabled memory v2 by default for fresh profiles and added support for importing external-agent memories into it. (#56211, #56414)

## Bug Fixes

- Fixed fresh TUI sessions to honor the server’s default approval reviewer when no explicit override is provided. (#56090)
- Kept TUI preferences editable and immediately applicable when execution settings are invalid. (#56091)
- Cancelled remote MCP tool requests when their local response futures are dropped. (#56132)
- Prevented queued agent messages from restarting work after an interrupt or a switch to Plan mode. (#56330)
- Stopped retrying when a provider reports that a model was not found, preserving its error message. (#56445)
- Closed a marketplace URL validation gap that could allow Git to connect to a different host than the one checked against allowed patterns. (#56263)

prs.title: Move the V8 Bazel build graph into Codex
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Move the V8 Bazel build graph into Codex

## What changed

- Replace the upstream V8 module and dependency bridge with a source repository rule and `third_party/v8/engine.BUILD.bazel`, wiring dependencies and Python generator inputs directly from Codex.
- Import source filegroups from the pinned upstream BUILD, rejecting missing boundaries, malformed sections, and unexpected compiled targets.
- Define fixed source feature selections in the engine BUILD while retaining release ABI, runtime, and CPU settings. Reuse upstream platform configuration and limit the build integration patch to `bazel/defs.bzl`.
- Document source inventory review and canary validation for V8 upgrades.

prs.title: Enforce V8 artifact profiles at Bazel target boundaries
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Enforce V8 artifact profiles at Bazel target boundaries

## Why

V8 source and release artifacts require different ABI and C++ runtime settings. Selecting a named artifact should also select its required settings, without callers coordinating separate sandbox, pointer compression, libc++, and CPU flags.

## What changed

- Add Bazel transitions for `source`, `release`, and `sandbox_release` profiles. Source builds use the sandbox ABI and workspace runtime; release pairs use Chromium's pinned runtime with their respective ABI.
- Select the V8 CPU from the artifact target and enforce matching target platform constraints.
- Make the underlying V8 settings unavailable as CLI flags and remove redundant configuration from release tooling and workflows.
- Select Darwin/Linux prebuilts solely through `rusty_v8_from_source`, keeping source archives and bindings paired when enabled.

prs.title: Surface automatic marketplace update failures as startup warnings
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Surface automatic marketplace update failures as startup warnings

## Why

Automatic marketplace update failures were only logged, leaving users without a visible startup warning.

## What changed

Send marketplace update errors and task startup failures through app-server warning notifications. Queue background warnings until a client initializes in both standalone and in-process servers, and centralize startup configuration warning delivery.

## Testing

Add a TUI integration test and snapshot covering two marketplace name mismatch failures, the warning count, and navigation between their details with `F2` and the arrow keys.

prs.title: Track CUA tool call starts and deduplicate lifecycle events
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Track CUA tool call starts and deduplicate lifecycle events

## What changed

Emit `codex_cua_tool_call_started` for `js` MCP calls on Node REPL-backed connectors. Include start time, tool identity, plugin and connector IDs, and available thread and response attribution without recording tool arguments.

Suppress duplicate starts and replayed completions for CUA calls while retaining the existing MCP completion event. A completion received without a start does not prevent a later valid lifecycle from being recorded.

## Testing

Add a lifecycle regression test covering missing starts, duplicate notifications, replay after completion, attribution fields, timestamps, and exclusion of tool arguments from serialized events.

- Add `.nvmrc` pinning Node.js to `24.22.1` and raise the root package's minimum Node.js version to match.

Clarify config loader APIs and share interactive login setup

prs.title: Integrate runtime authentication into model requests
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Integrate runtime authentication into model requests

## What changed

- Add opt-in runtime authentication through `ModelClient::with_runtime_auth`, requiring the provider and runtime manager to share the selected OpenAI credentials.
- Keep runtime identity, credentials, routing, and transport selection consistent for each request and its retries, signing a fresh assertion for each attempt.
- Apply authentication asynchronously to WebSocket handshakes, replace stale authentication headers, and reconnect when the runtime changes.
- Reject account, organization, or project selectors that conflict with the registered runtime, and preserve gateway OAuth composition.

## Testing

Add coverage for dual-header and assertion-only authentication, HTTP retries, runtime replacement and account switches, stale WebSocket headers, selector mismatches, gateway OAuth failures, transport revocation, and Realtime compatibility.

prs.title: Expose lifecycle timestamps on app-server thread items
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Expose lifecycle timestamps on app-server thread items

## What changed

- Add nullable `startedAtMs` and `completedAtMs` fields to `ThreadItem` in live notifications and turn history. Values are Unix milliseconds when recorded.
- Preserve recorded item times through history reconstruction, pagination, and resume, including command start times recorded during approval.
- Separate the Rust item payload into `ThreadItemPayload` while keeping the JSON payload flat, and update consumers, schemas, and generated TypeScript and Python types.

## Testing

Extend coverage for timestamp serialization, history reconstruction, paginated reads and resume, and persisted Python SDK items.

prs.title: Add scoped request-body secret substitution to MITM hooks
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add scoped request-body secret substitution to MITM hooks

## What changed

- Add `body_secret_substitution` actions to version 2 MITM configuration, replacing exact opaque placeholders with secrets from environment variables or files within the matching hook's scope.
- Bound body size, expansion, replacement count, and search work. Reject overlapping matches, compressed payloads, trailers, and supplied payload-integrity headers.
- Recompute `Content-Length` and substitute before SigV4 signing so signatures cover the transmitted body.

## Testing

Add coverage for markers split across chunks, expansion limits, invalid payloads, overlapping bindings, secret redaction, and search limits. Add a TLS forwarding test that verifies hook scope and independently checks the signature of the substituted body.

prs.title: Integrate config-server policies with startup and authentication
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Integrate config-server policies with startup and authentication

## What changed

- Use the managed configuration loader in CLI, exec, TUI, and app-server configuration flows so `requirements.toml` can select a config server.
- Sign in to the config server when needed during interactive TUI startup and CLI login, reload configuration after CLI sign-in, and clear config-server credentials on CLI logout.
- Preserve the app-server's config-server settings and refresh worker across OpenAI login and logout.
- Require config-server settings to be applied when loading CLI and doctor configuration.

## Testing

Add app-server integration tests using a local HTTPS config server to verify managed provider and instruction settings at startup, preservation across API-key login and logout, and cache reuse after restart and thread resume.

prs.title: Route FedRAMP API keys to government endpoints by default
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Route FedRAMP API keys to government endpoints by default

## Why

API keys with FedRAMP issuance markers previously used commercial endpoint defaults without a FedRAMP request header.

## What changed

- Recognize `sk-proj-fedramp-` and `sk-svcacct-fedramp-` prefixes as routing hints and send `X-OpenAI-Fedramp: true`, preserving the complete key for authentication.
- Select `https://gov.api.openai.com/v1` for default OpenAI API routing and `https://gov.chatgpt.com/backend-api/` for default ChatGPT backend requests, including model discovery and analytics.
- Preserve explicit endpoint overrides, including an explicitly configured commercial default URL.
- Resolve provider routing and authentication from the same credential snapshot, and apply key-dependent routing to realtime WebSocket startup.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for prefix recognition, unchanged key storage and authorization, provider credential precedence, endpoint overrides, credential rotation, model discovery, analytics routing, and realtime request preparation.

prs.title: Consolidate async header authentication in `apply_auth_headers`
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Consolidate async header authentication in `apply_auth_headers`

## What changed

Remove `AuthProvider::resolve_auth_headers` and use `apply_auth_headers` as the async interface for header-only authentication. Migrate providers, callers, and existing tests to the shared interface, passing an empty `HeaderMap` when only authentication headers are needed.

Document that providers may refresh credentials asynchronously and that callers must use the returned header map so providers can remove superseded credentials.

prs.title: Add constraint-aware standalone network proxy configuration
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add constraint-aware standalone network proxy configuration

## What changed

- Export `StaticNetworkProxyConfig` to parse and serialize network policy with constraints, and validate them before building proxy state.
- Add `--strict` and `from_slice_strict` for managed callers, requiring explicit `constraints` and rejecting unknown fields at every typed level. Default parsing permits top-level `metadata` and omitted constraints while still rejecting unknown policy fields.
- Match allowed Unix socket paths case-sensitively when validating constraints.
- Bound configuration file reads to the size limit plus one byte.

## Testing

Add coverage for constraint round trips, weakened policy rejection, exact socket path matching, parsing modes, and CLI flag selection. Exercise automatic MITM enablement through both parsers.

prs.title: Add optional names to untrusted additional context
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add optional names to untrusted additional context

## What changed

- Add an optional `name` to `AdditionalContextEntry` across the protocol, app-server schemas, and generated clients.
- Accept names matching `[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}` only for `untrusted` context. Reject invalid names and names on `application` context before admitting turn input, returning invalid-request errors from `turn/start` and `turn/steer`.
- Preserve existing model-input rendering and deduplicate context when only its name changes.

## Testing

Add coverage for valid name boundaries, callers that omit `name`, invalid-name rejection without admitting input, and deduplication across name changes.

Centralize unified exec output rendering

prs.title: Fail closed on unreadable glob search root metadata errors
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fail closed on unreadable glob search root metadata errors

## Why

Linux sandbox deny-glob expansion silently skipped search roots when metadata lookup failed, potentially discarding a deny rule.

## What changed

Return a fatal error with the search root and underlying error when metadata lookup fails, except for missing or non-directory roots, which still have no matches. Continue following directory symlinks.

## Testing

Add regression tests for symlink-loop metadata errors stopping expansion before scanning, absent and non-directory roots being skipped, and symlink roots expanding to both logical and canonical paths without ripgrep.

prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Allow advisory rollout budgets with optional limit enforcement

## What changed

Add `features.rollout_budget.enforce_limit`, defaulting to `true`. Setting it to `false` keeps shared usage accounting and budget reminders active while allowing turns to continue after the budget is exhausted.

## Testing

prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Add a credential file override for GCP provider authentication

## What changed

Support `model_providers.gcp.credential_file` as an absolute path to a Google Application Default Credentials (ADC) file. Pass it as `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` in the provider auth command's environment, retaining the override for token refreshes without changing the parent process environment.

Validate the path before merging GCP defaults and preserve the setting in thread configuration serialization.

## Testing

Add coverage for invalid paths, configuration round trips, separate provider token caches, and credential overrides retained after a `401` refresh. Include a Windows regression test for credential paths containing command metacharacters.

prs.title: Read unified exec output directly from stdout and stderr
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Read unified exec output directly from stdout and stderr

## What changed

Consume local stdout and stderr receivers directly with `tokio::select!`, removing the intermediate broadcast channel and its lag-related chunk skipping. Drain both streams until they close.

Pass `ExecOutputStream` through local and remote output collection to `OutputBuffers::push_chunk`, while retaining combined output buffers.

## Testing

Update output-buffer tests for the stream argument and exercise stderr chunks in pushed-event and replay test fixtures.

prs.title: Gate capability discovery V2 on executor version
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Gate capability discovery V2 on executor version

## Why

Executors older than `0.164.0` can advertise V2 discovery support without implementing the final contract. Enabling V2 also suppressed V1 discovery for incompatible executors, hiding selected capability roots and skills.

## What changed

Require both the V2 capability flag and an executor version of at least `0.164.0` before issuing `capabilities/discoverV2`. Share this compatibility check between session discovery and the exec-server client. Fall back to V1 when incompatible executors provide no V2 snapshots, clearing any previously stored V2 inventory.

## Testing

Add coverage for version boundaries, prereleases, missing and malformed versions, and transport recovery for compatible executors. Verify that an older executor retains selected plugins and skill instructions through V1 with V2 enabled.

prs.title: Preserve failed `write_stdin` calls in rollout trace replay
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Preserve failed `write_stdin` calls in rollout trace replay

## Why

Invalid model arguments to `write_stdin` represent a tool failure, but parsing them could fail rollout trace replay.

## What changed

Skip terminal operation creation when dispatched `write_stdin` arguments cannot be parsed or lack a usable `session_id`. Preserve the generic tool call and its error, including the original arguments, so replay can continue.

## Testing

Add a regression test covering malformed JSON and missing or null `session_id` values. Verify that replay retains the failed call's arguments and error without creating terminal operations or sessions.

prs.title: Classify rollout tool calls by their runtime handler
prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Classify rollout tool calls by their runtime handler

## Why

Tool interception and MCP aliases can route a requested callable to a different handler. Rollout traces need to reflect the handler that actually executes, including when an `exec_command` invocation is intercepted as `apply_patch`.

## What changed

Carry an explicit `ToolCallKind` in runtime-start events and use it to update the tool call's execution classification. This replaces MCP-specific payload inspection while preserving the original callable summary and invocation for intercepted patch and aliased MCP calls.

## Testing

Add a regression test verifying that an intercepted `exec_command` is recorded as `ApplyPatch`, retains its original summary and invocation, completes successfully, and creates no terminal operations or sessions.

prs.author: copyberry[bot]
prs.body:
Fix macOS standalone release pruning

## Why

macOS `lsof +D` can return status 1 even when it finds open files, causing release cleanup to be skipped. It can also escape non-ASCII installation paths, preventing full-path matching from recognizing releases in use.

## What changed

Accept `lsof` status 1 while preserving matches, and continue to reject other failures or any stderr. Match the installer-owned ASCII path suffix on macOS and recognize processes whose working directory is the release root. Apply these checks before and after moving a release for deletion.

## Testing

Add coverage for `lsof` exit statuses, output, and errors. Exercise release retention with a non-ASCII installation path and, on macOS, a process holding the release directory open.
